content.paragraph: In Sections 2.2 and 2.4 we investigated infinite limits and vertical asymptotes of a curve $$y = f(x)$$ . There we let $$x$$ approach a number and the result was that the values of $$y$$ became arbitrarily large (positive or negative). In this section we let $$x$$ become arbitrarily large (positive or negative) and see what happens to $$y$$ .

subsection.title: Evaluating Limits at Infinity
subsection.paragraph: Most of the Limit Laws that were given in Section 2.3 also hold for limits at infinity. It can be proved that the Limit Laws listed in Section 2.3 (with the exception of Laws 10 and 11 ) are also valid if “$$\left. x\rightarrow a \right.$$ ” is replaced by “$$\left. x\rightarrow\infty \right.$$ ” or “$$\left. x\rightarrow - \infty \right.$$ .” In particular, if we combine Laws 6 and 7 with the results of Example 2, we obtain the following important rule for calculating limits.

problem.paragraph: Evaluate the following limit and indicate which properties of limits are used at each stage.
Solution As $$x$$ becomes large, both numerator and denominator become large, so it isn’t obvious what happens to their ratio. We need to do some preliminary algebra.

To evaluate the limit at infinity of any rational function, we first divide both the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $$x$$ that occurs in the denominator. (We may assume that $$x \neq 0$$ , since we are interested only in large values of $$x$$ .) In this case the highest power of $$x$$ in the denominator is $$x^{2}$$ , so we have

paragraph.math: $$\begin{array}{l} {{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{3x^{2} - x - 2}{5x^{2} + 4x + 1}} = {\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\frac{3x^{2} - x - 2}{x^{2}}}{\frac{5x^{2} + 4x + 1}{x^{2}}} = \lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{3 - \frac{1}{x} - \frac{2}{x^{2}}}{5 + \frac{4}{x} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}}}} \\ {\phantom{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{3x^{2} - x - 2}{5x^{2} + 4x + 1}} = {\frac{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\left( {3 - \frac{1}{x} - \frac{2}{x^{2}}} \right)}{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\left( {5 + \frac{4}{x} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}} \right)}\qquad\left( {{by\ Limit\ Law}5} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{3x^{2} - x - 2}{5x^{2} + 4x + 1}} = {\frac{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}3 - \lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{x} - 2\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{x^{2}}}{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}5 + 4\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{x} + \lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{x^{2}}}\qquad\left( {{by}1,2,{and}3} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{3x^{2} - x - 2}{5x^{2} + 4x + 1}} = {\frac{3 - 0 - 0}{5 + 0 + 0}\qquad\left( {{by}8{and\ Theorem}5} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{3x^{2} - x - 2}{5x^{2} + 4x + 1}} = \frac{3}{5}} \end{array}$$

Evaluate $$\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\sin x$$ .

Solution As $$x$$ increases, the values of $$\sin x$$ oscillate between $$1$$ and $$- 1$$ infinitely often and so they don’t approach any definite number. Thus $$\lim_{x\rightarrow\infty}\sin x$$ does not exist.
